notes:
Lead profile: small SaaS support automation startup building a lightweight omnichannel inbox for SMB merchants.

What they care about (verbatim/highlights):
- 'Need tidy JSON outputs for downstream ticket routing — we will run deterministic parsers on top.'
- Fast turn-up, low ops overhead; prefer self-serve + public cloud.
- Cost-sensitive but willing to pay for consistent latency during peak business hours.

Technical summary / requirements:
- Primary workload: asynchronous support-agent + automated summarization of inbound tickets. Batch post-processing for nightly analytics.
- Secondary: tool-calling to open/close tickets in their system and fetch order metadata (webhook-style integrations).
- Latency targets: 200ms median for quick summarization (single-turn), 500ms p95 acceptable for complex ticket threads.
- Throughput: typical steady-state 5-10 qps; peaks up to 80-120 qps for short bursts (marketing campaigns).
- Model preference: open-model compatibility; likely will test 7B/13B quantized variants first.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper model under cost pressure; also prefer regional routing to NA.
- Security: SSO for internal admin, audit logs for actions, token retention controls. No air-gapped requirement.

Commercial notes:
- SMB budget — estimated ARR small. Customer expects to start on pay-as-you-go hosted API; potential Dedicated only if volume justifies.

Recent quotes / paraphrases from call:
- 'If we can get predictable latency and an easy webhook for tool-calls, we'll onboard the first 50 merchants fast.'
- 'We don't want to manage infra; hosted API is ideal.'

Open questions / pending items:
